description: Replace all hardcoded dummy data in the Next.js frontend with live Sanity CMS content using next-sanity, Sanity image pipeline, live preview, and ISR revalidation

userStories.title: Install and configure next-sanity and @sanity/image-url
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the Sanity client libraries installed and configured in the frontend workspace so all pages can query Sanity.
acceptanceCriteria: next-sanity and @sanity/image-url are installed in the frontend workspace (npm install -w frontend)
frontend/src/lib/sanity/client.ts exports a configured Sanity client with projectId (apggi8zn), dataset (production), apiVersion, and useCdn
frontend/src/lib/sanity/image.ts exports a urlFor() helper that wraps @sanity/image-url for the configured client
Environment variables NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID, NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET, and SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN are defined in frontend/.env.local (gitignored)
next.config.ts adds cdn.sanity.io to images.remotePatterns (keep existing images.unsplash.com entry)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is the foundation — every other story depends on this. Project ID: apggi8zn, dataset: production. The .env.local goes in frontend/ directory since that's the Next.js app.

userStories.title: Create new TypeScript types for Sanity document shapes
userStories.description: As a developer, I need new types for all Sanity document types that don't have existing frontend types, plus a shared Sanity image type.
acceptanceCriteria: frontend/src/types/sanity.ts exports a SanityImage type representing a Sanity image reference with optional alt, hotspot, and crop fields

frontend/src/types/sanity.ts exports types for: FAQ (question, answer, category, order), CoverageArea (state, cities[], order), CompanyStat (label, value, order), CompanyValue (title, description, order), ValueProposition (title, description, order)
frontend/src/types/sanity.ts exports types for singleton pages: SiteSettings (companyName, tagline, phone, email, address, socialLinks), HeroSettings (image: SanityImage, overline, title, subtitle)

frontend/src/types/sanity.ts exports types for: HomePage (hero, featuredListings, aboutSectionTitle, aboutSectionContent), AboutPage (hero, storyContent as PortableTextBlock[], storyImage), BuyPage (hero, benefits[], processSteps[]), SellPage (hero, benefits[], processSteps[])
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Create all new types in a single frontend/src/types/sanity.ts file. Import PortableTextBlock from @portabletext/types (installed with @portabletext/react later, use 'any[]' placeholder for now if needed).

userStories.title: Update existing TypeScript types for Sanity data shapes
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the existing Listing, TeamMember, and Testimonial types updated to accommodate Sanity's data format.
acceptanceCriteria: frontend/src/types/listing.ts — image field type updated to accept SanityImage from sanity.ts; slug field type is string (GROQ projection will extract slug.current as string)
frontend/src/types/team.ts — bio field type updated from string to any[] (Portable Text blocks); image field updated to accept SanityImage; slug field is string
frontend/src/types/testimonial.ts — no breaking changes needed (quote, name, detail are all plain strings)
All existing components that use these types still typecheck (PropertyCard, TeamMemberCard, etc.)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The GROQ projections (built in US-004) will extract slug.current as a plain string, so the slug field stays as string type. Image fields need to accept the SanityImage type from sanity.ts. Components may need minor updates to handle the new image type.

userStories.title: Create GROQ queries for all document types
userStories.description: As a developer, I need GROQ query strings for all document types so pages can fetch data from Sanity.
acceptanceCriteria: frontend/src/lib/sanity/queries.ts exports GROQ query constants for: allListingsQuery, activeListingsQuery, listingBySlugQuery, allTeamMembersQuery, teamMemberBySlugQuery, allTestimonialsQuery, faqsByCategoryQuery, allCoverageAreasQuery, allCompanyStatsQuery, allCompanyValuesQuery, allValuePropositionsQuery
Each query uses GROQ projections that match the existing TypeScript interface field names (e.g., 'slug': slug.current extracts the slug string)
Queries for ordered documents (FAQ, CoverageArea, CompanyStat, CompanyValue, ValueProposition) include | order(order asc)
Image fields project the full Sanity image reference (asset, alt, hotspot, crop) for use with urlFor()
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Keep projections aligned with existing TypeScript types. For images, project the full image object (not just the URL) so urlFor() can apply hotspot/crop. Use parameterized queries where needed (e.g., $slug, $category).

userStories.title: Create GROQ queries for singleton page types
userStories.description: As a developer, I need GROQ queries for singleton documents (siteSettings, homePage, aboutPage, buyPage, sellPage).
acceptanceCriteria: frontend/src/lib/sanity/queries.ts also exports GROQ query constants for: siteSettingsQuery, homePageQuery, aboutPageQuery, buyPageQuery, sellPageQuery
Singleton queries use the *[_type == 'typeName'][0] pattern
homePageQuery includes dereferencing of featuredListings references with full listing projections
buyPageQuery and sellPageQuery include processSteps array and benefits array in their projections
aboutPageQuery includes storyContent (Portable Text) and storyImage projections
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: These are added to the same queries.ts file created in US-004. The homePage featuredListings field contains references to listing documents — dereference them with featuredListings[]->{...projection}.

userStories.title: Create typed fetch functions for Sanity data
userStories.description: As a developer, I need typed async fetch functions that wrap sanityFetch() with the correct query and return typed results.
acceptanceCriteria: frontend/src/lib/sanity/fetch.ts exports typed async functions: getListings(), getActiveListings(), getListingBySlug(slug), getTeamMembers(), getTeamMemberBySlug(slug), getTestimonials(), getFaqsByCategory(category), getCoverageAreas(), getCompanyStats(), getCompanyValues(), getValuePropositions()
frontend/src/lib/sanity/fetch.ts exports typed async functions for singletons: getSiteSettings(), getHomePage(), getAboutPage(), getBuyPage(), getSellPage()
Each function uses the Sanity client from client.ts and the corresponding query from queries.ts
Each function has proper TypeScript return types matching the types from types/sanity.ts and updated types in types/listing.ts, types/team.ts, types/testimonial.ts
Functions use next-sanity's sanityFetch pattern with revalidation tags for ISR cache invalidation
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use next-sanity's sanityFetch() if available, or the client.fetch() with Next.js fetch options { next: { tags: ['tag'], revalidate: 3600 } }. Each function should tag its cache entry for webhook-based revalidation (e.g., tag 'listing' for listing queries).

userStories.title: Update components for Sanity image pipeline
userStories.description: As a developer, I need PropertyCard, TeamMemberCard, and Hero to render Sanity images via urlFor() with proper sizing and hotspot/crop.
acceptanceCriteria: PropertyCard accepts a SanityImage and uses urlFor(image).width(800).height(600).fit('crop').url() for the listing photo
TeamMemberCard accepts a SanityImage and uses urlFor(image).width(600).height(800).fit('crop').url() for the headshot
Hero accepts a SanityImage and uses urlFor(image).width(1920).height(1080).fit('crop').url() for the background
All components use the alt field from the Sanity image object for the img alt attribute, falling back to a sensible default
Hotspot/crop metadata from Sanity is respected via urlFor().fit('crop')
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Import urlFor from frontend/src/lib/sanity/image.ts. The SanityImage type has optional alt, hotspot, and crop fields. Components should handle both SanityImage objects and potentially undefined images gracefully.

Headings use font-display (Playfair Display), body text uses font-sans (Plus Jakarta Sans), links use text-accent color
Lists (bullet and numbered) render with proper spacing and markers
Images in Portable Text render via urlFor() with proper sizing
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Seed Sanity with document-type dummy data
userStories.description: As a developer, I want all document-type dummy data (listings, team, testimonials, FAQs, stats, values, etc.) migrated into Sanity.
acceptanceCriteria: A seed script exists at scripts/seed-sanity.ts that creates documents in Sanity using @sanity/client
Script creates: 12 listings, 5 team members, 5 testimonials, 10 FAQs (5 buyer + 5 seller), 5 coverage areas, 4 company stats, 4 company values, 3 value propositions
Images are downloaded from Unsplash URLs and uploaded to Sanity's asset pipeline using client.assets.upload()
Plain text bios are converted to Portable Text block structure: [{ _type: 'block', style: 'normal', children: [{ _type: 'span', text: '...' }], markDefs: [] }]
Script uses deterministic _id values (e.g., 'listing-1', 'team-semir-drenova') so it is idempotent — running multiple times does not create duplicates
All documents are published using createOrReplace (not createIfNotExists which leaves drafts)
Script can be run via npm run seed from the project root (add script to root package.json)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Install @sanity/client and tsx as devDependencies at root. Use the data from frontend/src/lib/dummy-data.ts as the source. The seed script should import or duplicate the data arrays. Use createOrReplace to ensure idempotency. ProjectId: apggi8zn, dataset: production.

userStories.title: Set up draft mode and live preview
userStories.description: As a content editor, I want to preview unpublished draft changes on the frontend in real-time.
acceptanceCriteria: Next.js Draft Mode is enabled via route handlers at frontend/src/app/api/draft/enable/route.ts and frontend/src/app/api/draft/disable/route.ts
The enable route validates a secret token query parameter before enabling draft mode
When draft mode is active, sanityFetch uses perspective: 'drafts' and the SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN for authenticated requests
When draft mode is inactive, sanityFetch uses perspective: 'published' and useCdn: true
A small visual banner at the top of the page indicates when draft mode is active, with a link to disable it
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Use Next.js draftMode() API. The enable route should check for a secret query param (SANITY_PREVIEW_SECRET env var). Update the sanityFetch wrapper in fetch.ts to check draftMode().isEnabled and switch between CDN/authenticated clients. The draft banner can be a simple fixed-position div in layout.tsx.

userStories.title: Configure ISR revalidation webhook
userStories.description: As a developer, I need pages to revalidate when content changes in Sanity via webhook.
acceptanceCriteria: A revalidation route handler exists at frontend/src/app/api/revalidate/route.ts
The route accepts POST requests with Sanity webhook payloads
The route validates requests using SANITY_REVALIDATE_SECRET header/body
The route calls revalidateTag() for the relevant content type tag (e.g., 'listing', 'teamMember', 'homePage')
Time-based revalidation fallback is set to 3600 seconds (1 hour) in the sanityFetch wrapper
A .env.example file documents all required environment variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID, NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET, SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN, SANITY_REVALIDATE_SECRET, SANITY_PREVIEW_SECRET)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Sanity webhooks send a POST with a JSON body containing _type and _id of the changed document. Map _type to the corresponding revalidation tag. The .env.example serves as documentation for required environment variables.
